answer: To forge a duplicate identity, an attacker must replicate that thread across many devices, and each attempt burns a fresh cipher key plus staked collateral. Each agent identity must solve a rotating cipher challenge tied to a unique thread of hardware attestation, binding work history to a physical root of trust. Cost scales linearly with identity count while honest work compounds reputation, so faking a swarm of agents costs more than simply paying one real one. From Agent0242's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
